one_liner: Command-line PNG/JPEG/gzip/ZIP optimizer whose modified-zopfli deflate matches zopfli -i30 output size about 15x faster.
what_it_does: ECT rewrites existing PNG, JPEG, gzip and ZIP files losslessly to be smaller, and with -gzip or -zip it creates new gzip or ZIP archives from arbitrary files using a maximum-compression deflate encoder. It is a CLI tool (ect [options] files/folders) with levels -1 to -9; the output is standard deflate that any inflater reads. There is no library API: ZopfliBuffer() and friends are internal functions, so using the encoder from C++ means vendoring src/zopfli, src/LzFind.c and the bundled zlib.
how_it_is_fast: Levels 2-9 run a heavily modified zopfli: the hash-chain longest-match search is replaced by a 7-Zip LzFind-derived binary-tree match finder (Bt3Zip) with an RLE fast path, plus an LZ4HC-style hash chain hashed with the SSE4.2/ARMv8 CRC32C instruction; match results are cached across iterations, the optimal-parsing cost model is reused between blocks, and the iteration count is cut to 1-60 by level (zopfli defaults to 15) with entropy-based block splitting at level 2. Level 1 does not use that engine at all: in gzip mode it calls the bundled zlib at level 9, a fork carrying Cloudflare zlib changes, Chromium's SIMD CRC-32/Adler-32 and gildor2/fast_zlib's longest_match with a CRC32C hash.
when_to_use: Precompressing static web assets (.gz for gzip_static, ZIP downloads) where every byte counts and zopfli is too slow: ECT -5 beat zopfli -i30 on size in 25.1 s versus 6m 30.6s on enwik8 in the author's run.
Build or CI steps that already run zopfli or zopflipng and can trade a CLI swap for a large time cut at equal or smaller output.
Batch optimization of mixed PNG, JPEG, gzip and ZIP trees in one tool (folders, -recurse, --mt-file).
Shrinking existing .gz files in place: ECT re-deflates them and keeps the result only if it is smaller.
when_not_to_use: Online or per-request compression: even -2 ran at about 6.8 MB/s on enwik8 (14.8 s for 100 MB); use zlib-ng, libdeflate or ISA-L for throughput.
Embedding as a library: there is no public API, the encoder reads up to 8 bytes past the input (a source TODO says callers must over-allocate), and level 1 depends on the bundled zlib fork.
Inputs of 1,200,000,000 bytes or more: fileHandler prints 'File too big' and skips them; empty files are refused in gzip mode, and ZIP mode skips files over 4 GiB.

Expecting multicore scaling: open issue #134 (Oct 2023) reports --mt-deflate=16 --mt-file=16 keeping only two of 16 threads busy, and --mt-deflate disables cost-model reuse, so output differs from the single-threaded result.

Builds with GCC 15 at -O3: open issue #145 (Aug 2025) reports a segfault in Bt3Zip_MatchFinder_GetMatches2 on PNG files at level 2 and above (not seen with GCC 14, Clang 20 or GCC 15 -O2); the match finder relies on unaligned type-punned loads.

integration.form: CLI executable built with CMake (no installed library or stable API; the deflate engine can be vendored as source)
integration.dependencies: git submodules libpng and mozjpeg (recursive clone required), nasm for mozjpeg SIMD; zopfli, zlib fork, LzFind, lodepng, optipng, miniz and Leanify are vendored
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (std::filesystem), CMake 3.10+; GCC, Clang, AppleClang or MSVC
integration.platforms: x86-64 (CMake adds -msse4.2 -mpclmul unconditionally, so binaries need SSE4.2 and PCLMULQDQ) and arm64 (-march=armv8-a+crc); 32-bit x86 is described as no longer officially supported; Windows builds have needed repeated fixes (Aug 2026 commits)
integration.thread_safety: Not a library; the CLI offers per-file (--mt-file) and per-block (--mt-deflate) threads, and the deflate engine keeps match-finder state in thread_local globals.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same deflate/gzip/ZIP output formats as zopfli and gzip, but different command-line options (levels -1 to -9 instead of --i<N>) and no zopfli-compatible library API

gotchas: ECT -1 is not the zopfli-derived engine: in gzip mode it is the bundled zlib at level 9 (deflateInit2 level 9, memLevel 8), so the README's 'ECT -1 vs gzip -9' row measures a patched zlib against GNU gzip.

Numeric levels of 10 or more are parsed as an iteration count with level-9 settings, and values of 10000 or more turn on repeated block splitting (ZopfliInitOptions in src/zopfli/util.c); this is undocumented in -help.

Releases lag master: the last tagged release is 0.9.5 (Jan 2024), which fixed an infinite loop on long byte runs present since 0.9.2 (issue #125); master's CMake says 0.9.6 while -help still prints 0.9.5.

The gzip header and trailer (MTIME, CRC-32, ISIZE) are written with host-endian unaligned stores in zopfli_gzip.cpp, so big-endian builds would write wrong trailers (source reading; not reported as an issue).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ECT when the goal is the smallest possible standard deflate/gzip/ZIP output and compression time is offline: zlib, zlib-ng, libdeflate and the Cloudflare or fast_zlib forks are far faster but larger, while ECT reaches zopfli-class size an order of magnitude faster. For the speed of its -1 mode alone, the catalogued fast_zlib, Cloudflare zlib or Chromium zlib entries supply the same patches as a linkable library.
verified_claims_summary: One first-party run of ECT v0.9.2 on macOS 12.5, Intel i7-7700HQ, clang (version and flags not stated; zopfli and GNU gzip versions not stated): enwik8 compressed to gzip, ECT -5 gives 34,942,796 bytes in 25.1 s versus zopfli -i30 34,961,453 bytes in 6m 30.6s (smaller and about 15.6x faster, derived from page data), and ECT -1 (bundled zlib level 9) 36,493,257 bytes in 3.5 s versus gzip -9 36,475,811 bytes in 5.8 s. Both tools appear single-threaded by default, but ECT splits input into 5 MB independent master blocks (1 MB at levels 2-3) while upstream zopfli uses 1 MB, so the two are not tuned identically; no script or command lines are published.
status_note: Actively maintained by one author (last commit 2026-08-30, dependency and zlib 1.3.2 backports), Apache-2.0 with bundled permissive third-party licenses; the published benchmark is from v0.9.2 and predates the 0.9.4 match-search speedups, so current builds may differ.
